value.body: A two-year master's in performing arts (M.P.A.) or music (M.Mus.). It deepens training in one art form — vocal or instrumental music, dance or theatre — alongside theory, history, research methods and teaching practice. It is the usual step towards UGC-NET, a PhD and college teaching.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree, usually in music or performing arts; some universities also take other graduates with recognised training in the art form. Admission is through the university's own entrance and practical test, or CUET-PG at central universities.

value.title: At a glance
items: Most programmes include a practical or performance component in every semester.
Graduates can sit UGC-NET in Music or Performing Arts for assistant professor posts and JRF.
Many students continue to perform or teach privately while studying.

value.note: Programme rows 'M.P.A. - Master of Performing Arts' and 'M.Mus. - Master of Music'. AISHE counts responding institutions only; coverage varies by year, so part of any change can reflect reporting rather than real growth.
